assessments.reasoning: The official mirror’s 3.46.0 tag links to the pinned revision and parse.y matched the expected raw digest. Lines 203–214 attach the option set to the parenthesized form and recursively combine comma-delimited option flags.

challenge.method: I confirmed the official mirror’s release tag and traced both CREATE TABLE productions. I tested both option orders, removed the comma and challenged the separation of the AS SELECT production. https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/releases/tag/version-3.46.0 I compiled the project’s 3.46.0 amalgamation with loadable extensions disabled and exercised only an in-memory database. The amalgamation’s sqlite3.c SHA3-256 matched the 3.46.0 release log. The executable reported source ID 96c92aba00c8375bc32fafcdf12429c58bd8aabfcadab6683e35bbb9cdebf19e. https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-3460000.zip
challenge.results: Both mixed-case comma-separated orders succeeded and registered both flags. The adjacent options without a comma failed. The AS SELECT path has no table option set. A trailing STRICT can still be a SELECT result alias: that example produced a column named STRICT with both table-option states clear. An explicit alias followed by STRICT produced a syntax error.

limitations: The implementation evidence concerns pinned 3.46.0 parser syntax. A primary key and acceptable column type were provided for the successful examples so later table validation could run.
The AS SELECT form uses a separate production and can accept an alias that looks like a table-option keyword.
